cells.tense: You sit here with the pen, and what you tend is being fed without being rushed.
cells.act: surrender the outcome and keep the act
cells.ask: Keep bringing something along for a few days without checking how it's going. No tally of whether it took. Just the doing.
cells.core:
You can tend without squeezing. Something in your care is developing on a schedule you didn't set, and you hold the conditions steady — give it what it needs and let it arrive when it arrives. You don't stand over it asking whether it grew today. That is why it grows. This is the shape when it's working.

Where it bends you now: staying steady starts to feel like proof is missing. Nothing has to be demonstrated for this to hold. Set the scorecard down for a stretch — did it take, was it enough, are they grateful — and the work keeps its worth. Surrender the outcome and keep the doing. What you carry gets lighter when it stops having to report.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the conditions steady, and it grows on a schedule you didn't set.
cells.place: on ground where things get weighed side by side

cells.tense: You are already reaching into a future that hasn't arrived, arranging what isn't here yet.
cells.act: let the path show itself instead of forcing clarity
cells.ask: Go one step into the stretch you're bracing hardest against, using only what you can see now. Build nothing past that step.
cells.core:
Care has become control here. You can read what someone or something is about to need, so you get there early — arranging, preventing, carrying the load before it lands. Outsiders call it devotion. Inside, it's a loop that won't close, because the future keeps needing something handled.

Bracing is not the same as loving, and stopping one doesn't stop the other. Walk toward what you care about with only enough light for the next step — not the whole road. The fog you keep trying to burn away is where things you haven't met are still being made. Let it stay fog. Let the path show itself, and watch what keeps standing without your hand on it.
cells.sheetLine: You're organizing a future nobody can write yet.
cells.place: on ground where things get weighed side by side

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you quietly stopped opening some time back.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Notice what you genuinely want out here, just to yourself, then take one small step toward it. Not what's fair — what you want.
cells.core:
On ground where things get weighed, something in you went quiet. It reads as independence — contained, no one needed — but it's a door you don't knock on anymore. Nothing you wanted got cleared with anyone, so wanting less started looking like the fair correction. The draw is still there, on the far side.

There is a way through. Pay attention to what you actually want, then move one step toward it — not the need, just the wish. Let yourself want it plainly, to yourself, with nobody watching. Wanting doesn't obligate anyone else. It's the door opening on ground where you're free to want. Take the step while the fairness question is still open.
cells.sheetLine: You keep a door shut and call the quiet independence.

cells.tense: You keep holding a shape handed to you, pen down in a room you didn't write.
cells.act: stop holding what no longer serves
cells.ask: Find what you're carrying here because you were standing there, not because it was handed to you. Put it down and keep your hands off it.
cells.core:
People turn to you as the one who holds things, and you hold them, without signing on. What needs tending gets brought and you tend it, and somewhere in that the role attached to you as if it had been there from the start. It feels like love, and it feels like running out at the same time, because you've been carrying a load you didn't choose.

What gets you out is small, not loud. Find one piece of the load that isn't yours — one you're holding because you were standing there — and stop holding it. On your side. Let your hands be free for a while and feel what's there. You may pick things up on purpose again later. For now put this piece down.
cells.sheetLine: You hold a role you didn't pick, and it can be set down.
cells.place: on ground where things get weighed side by side

attempts.check: The record supports the card as care for what is growing — tending, conditions for growth, patient attention — not as warmth or as being a kind person. The reader could reasonably object that this is a description of a gardener, not of them, because tending plants is the most literal reading of the card; the core renders it as care for development in a person's own life. The ask survives being wrong: releasing one thing gripped is useful whether or not the person understands themselves as a cultivator. The sentence serving me more than them: any line that praises care back to a person who is being drained by it.
